clauses.reason: The sole command revokes, by the words of the order, all Executive orders or parts thereof establishing airspace reservations within the continental limits of the United States except the District of Columbia, and the order does not apply to Alaska or the Panama Canal Zone. The command operated when the order issued on December 6, 1941 and was thereby exhausted; its result, the revocation, survives as an accrued effect. EO 10768 of May 16, 1958 recites that EO 7138 was revoked as to its other airspace reservations by this order, which shows the revocation took effect, but it does not revoke or amend this order and is a later event, not an end. The order states no effective date other than its date; filing in the Federal Register was December 9, 1941.

research_rationale:
The registered working text is the Federal Register text layer of EO 8961 (6 FR 6325, Federal Register of December 10, 1941; machine-extracted, original page images not inspected). The order is dated December 6, 1941 and contains one command: that all Executive orders or parts thereof establishing airspace reservations within the continental limits of the United States, except the District of Columbia, are revoked, with a closing sentence that it does not apply to Alaska or to the Panama Canal Zone. The command revokes by its own words and was performed when the order issued, so it was exhausted on December 6, 1941. A revocation order's command is spent on performance; its result, the revocation of the reached orders, is the surviving effect. Evidence that the revocation operated: EO 10768 of May 16, 1958 states that Executive Order No. 7138 was revoked as to its other airspace reservations by this order. EO 10768 recites this order and revokes EO 7138; it does not revoke or amend EO 8961 and is recorded as a later event, not an end. The Federal Register filing date was December 9, 1941 and publication December 10, 1941; the signing date is recorded because the order states no other effective date.
